<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 873151021f640a7a2b8675f2c38ff10ec8a7230b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7b2581304820cd8e9fc1b9ad336b67ba6b42ada5`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23272 (body, triage `6147613353`, claim `6166328411`, os-dev-report `6169637194`), PR #23496 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the earlier head `d88df525c`, the touched files at that head), the one-commit delta `d88df525c..7b2581304` (`compare` API: one file, +2/-1), and the check-runs on `7b2581304` (read once). Card #23270's body was read for the shape list the triage pin names. This record supersedes the one rendered on `d88df525c`.

### ① Derived judgments

**Delta `d88df525c` → `7b2581304` (commit `7b2581304`, `docs(spec): …`):** `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` lines 25-27 only — the stale "Internal: not re-exported by `data/index.ts`." sentence becomes "Public: re-exported from `@objectstack/spec/data`, with the field predicate `isControlledByParentMasterField` it counts." No code token changes; the import line and `refuseControlledByParentWithoutOneMaster` are untouched. **Right** — it closes the one reviewer finding of the earlier record, and the file is in the claim's surface. Every judgment below is carried forward unchanged, since the delta touches no export, baseline, test or lint source.

**Public surface widened — `@objectstack/spec/data` only (`export * from './controlled-by-parent-master'`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts:366`).** The module holds exactly four exports, and `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain exactly those four and remove nothing, so the baselines say what the diff publishes:

1. `controlledByParentMasterRefusal(objectName: unknown, sharingModel: unknown, fields: unknown): ControlledByParentMasterRefusal | undefined` — **right.** Pre-existing body, already the judge `ObjectSchema`'s `refuseControlledByParentWithoutOneMaster` (`object.zod.ts:2002-2011`) calls; the only body change swaps the inline `type === 'master_detail' && required === true` filter for the new field predicate, so the verdict, `path` and `message` on every shape are unchanged. `undefined` for a non-`controlled_by_parent` model, for a non-map `fields`, and for the satisfying shape; this is the "one predicate" the triage asked for, at object level, and a producer asks `=== undefined`. Reachable through the return: `path` (`'fields' | 'sharingModel'`), `shape`, `masterDetails`, `requiredLookups`, `message` — all readonly, no schema or zod object leaks.
2. `isControlledByParentMasterField(field: unknown): boolean` — **right.** New, total over `unknown` (null/primitive → `false`), spells `master_detail` + `required === true` once; the refusal counts with it, the lint filters with it. It is the field-level half the lint needs (per-candidate `reference`, array-form fields) without changing lint findings — the PR's "why two" explanation holds on the diff: reading only the object verdict would drop the `refOf` filter and the per-candidate listing the two lint rule ids are pinned on.
3. `ControlledByParentMasterShape` (type) and `ControlledByParentMasterRefusal` (interface) — **right.** They are the return type of export 1; publishing the function without them would make the return un-nameable by a consumer.

**Landing spot vs. triage direction (`6147613353`: one predicate, in `object.zod.ts`, read by `ObjectSchema` and lint, pinned on #23270's shapes).** Judged **right with the dev's deviation.** The rule's owning module on `main` is `controlled-by-parent-master.ts` (#23387 moved it there; `object.zod.ts` only calls it), and the claim's file surface already names that module as the export's home. Re-exporting from the owner rather than duplicating in `object.zod.ts` is the "one rule, one spelling" rationale the triage gives. Two exports instead of one: the object-level predicate is export 1; export 2 is the count it is made of, and it is what lets the lint read the spec without altering pinned findings. Both `ObjectSchema` and lint now read the spec module, which is the drift guarantee the direction asks for. The runtime's `resolveCbpRelation` (plugin-security) keeps its own reading; the direction names only the parse and the lint, so that is outside this card and correctly left.

**Accept-set changes in `packages/spec`: none.** `object.zod.ts` carries only the comment edit; the refusal function's verdict table is the same outcome on every input. The new pin (`controlled-by-parent-master.test.ts`) holds the export equal to `ObjectSchema.safeParse` on verdict, path and message for each #23270 shape (`several-required-masters`, `several-masters`, `master-not-required` with `required: false` and omitted, `required-lookup-only`, `no-master`), the two satisfying shapes (accepted whole), and the three other sharing models — the triage pin as stated.

**`@objectstack/lint` findings: unchanged.** `cbpMasterCandidates` (`validate-security-posture.ts:346-350`) goes from `f.type === 'master_detail' && f.required === true && refOf(f)` to `isControlledByParentMasterField(f) && refOf(f)` — identical truth table (the predicate is the same two comparisons; `recordsOf` still feeds both map and array forms). Its `.map` (field/type/master), `resolveCbpRelation`'s `length === 1`, `pushCbpNoRelation`, `pushCbpAmbiguousRelation` and every rule id, path and message text are not in the diff. No lint test case was edited except the #5017 receiver meta-test row. The import edge `@objectstack/lint` → `@objectstack/spec/data` already existed (`referenceCarrierOf`), so no new dependency.

**#5017 receiver meta-test (`validate-security-posture.test.ts:1509-1513`):** the `f` row drops `required` — **right.** At the head the lint file has no remaining `.required` read (grep on the head file: zero hits), so the row now states the file's actual reads; the comment records why.

**Mirror/baseline obligations:** `api-surface` and `export-origins` regenerated in the PR (+4/+4, 0 removed). `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Flag docs affected by code changes` are `success` on this head.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23272-export-cbp-master-predicate.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: patch` — **matches the diff.** spec adds four exports to a published subpath and removes or alters nothing (minor, not patch; not major since no accept/refuse or export change). lint swaps an internal filter for an imported one with no finding change (patch). The changeset body names both exports, the `undefined` semantics, the producer's call shape, and that no shape's acceptance changes — accurate to the code. The delta is a comment and needs no changeset change. `Check Changeset`: success.

`Clause-②: yes` — present in the PR body, the changeset, and the claim; correct, since `@objectstack/spec/data` is a published entry (`package.json` `exports["./data"]`) and this PR widens it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions`: none. Dev `deviations`, each judged:

- Model-free commit trailer (`Co-authored-by: Claude`) because pre-push refuses a model id — **answered**: repo rule (AGENTS.md) over the harness reminder.
- Zero label writes; skip-changeset not applied because a changeset ships — **answered**: correct, and the dispatch named no label.
- Read cloud's `sharing-model.ts` via REST after a read-only `add_repo` — **answered**: a read to confirm the producer's call shape; nothing written to cloud.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`, judged:

- plugin-security `resolveCbpRelation` keeps its own master reading (carrier: none) — **accepted as out of scope**: the triage direction names only the parse and the lint; the lint's doc-comment at the head says so explicitly. Not escalated.
- cloud's `defaultSharingModel` counts `required !== false` (omitted → master), which `ObjectSchema` refuses as `master-not-required` — **correctly routed to the cloud seat** (cloud#2865); adopting export 1 is cloud's change.

Reviewer findings:

- The earlier record's one finding (stale "Internal: not re-exported" comment in `object.zod.ts`) is **closed by the delta**; no stale copy of the old claim remains in the files this PR touches (`conversions/refused-shapes.ts:47` describes that module's own internal status, which is still true).
- The brief's note says "two new public exports"; the diff publishes two functions **and** their two types (four `api-surface` entries). The types are the functions' signature, not extra surface, and the changeset names them. No action.
- The PR body's claim "all lint findings, paths and texts are unchanged" is **verified on the diff** (the only lint source change is the one filter expression plus a doc-comment); it is not taken from the dev's report.
